_marker: THE NAMED DIVERGENCES — every place the documented chain does NOT re-derive the committed corpus, with the reviewed cause. Read by scripts/corpus-reproducible-check.ts: an UNNAMED divergence refuses, and a row whose divergence has since been FIXED refuses too (a stale row is as dead as a missing one). Rows are not permission to drift — they are the admission, on the record, that a fact in the corpus came from somewhere the chain cannot reach.

polaris.cause: HAND-EDITED PROMOTED CONTRACTS WITH NO AUTHORED-FACTS LEDGER — and the capture half now proves the edits are the WHOLE story: polaris's twelve capture records re-derive 12/12 from its committed seed + config + sandbox, so nothing upstream is wrong. The break is entirely between the record and the contract. polaris is the one library whose ds-library.json names no `authored` file, and eight of its committed contracts carry edits the promoter does not produce: developed defaults (avatar `initials: "TP"` and `withInitials: true`, progress-bar `progress: 40`), FC-ENUM-HOLE (button `tone` gains the developed `default` value and its `{variant}.none` paint paths), FC-SVG-ROTATION (spinner glyphs gain `transform: rotate(90deg)`), console-loop VISUAL fixes (checkbox/radio-button backdrops swap minted `tokensByProp` for literal per-axis border+fill; the indeterminate glyph's `fill` is rebound to icon-6 white), a changed sample string (checkbox "Save this product" -> "Save this information"), and the minted leaves that go orphan or appear because of those. Each edit names its own cause inline in the contract, so none is a mystery about WHAT — but none is an INPUT, so the chain cannot produce them and `promote-generalization` has never covered polaris. The door that would carry them already exists (packages/cli/src/promote.ts authored facts: `edit` for the enum/default/description moves, `set.fields` for `literalsByProp` and `meter`, `set.declared` for the glyph rotation, `add` for the FC-ENUM-HOLE enum value, `prune` for the leaves that go orphan). Routing them is a bounded, mechanical round of its own and is NOT done here; this row exists so the gap is machine-checked rather than silent.  ROW DELETED 2026-08-26 (census/stack-to-main): `tokens/polaris-minted.dtcg.json` no longer diverges. Verified by running the gate's OWN promote into a temp tree and comparing per file — the artifact is PRODUCED, COMMITTED and BYTE-IDENTICAL, not merely un-compared (the tokens/ half of this checker walks the PRODUCED directory, so a committed file the promoter stopped emitting would silently leave the diverging set; this one is emitted). The `prune` clause above described the promoter removing minted leaves that go orphan when the checkbox/radio-button backdrops swap to literal paint; the promoter now emits the file with those leaves intact, so its output equals the committed bytes and there is nothing to name. Whether it OUGHT to prune them is a different instrument's question and is owned by the `minted-leaves-bind-to-something` ratchet (polaris sits at its committed baseline of 619 unreferenced leaves); it is not re-hidden here.

mui.cause: 2026-09-04, THE CssBaseline MOUNT CORRECTION. extract/computed/configs/mui.json wrapped every capture in <ThemeProvider> but never mounted <CssBaseline />, which is what puts the theme's typography on the document, so any component inheriting its face from body captured in the UA serif. Measured before: 13 of 32 mui captures carried NO Roboto stack in any font-family read, and mui was the only library in the corpus with any component whose reads were entirely UA defaults. After re-capturing 31 of 32 with CssBaseline mounted, all 13 carry one. The promotions therefore re-derive differently across the library. THE CURATED-FACT GUARD WAS RUN over all 31 committed contracts against their re-promotion and reports NO LOSSES: every divergence adds or reshapes, none deletes a curated value — which is the check that exists because a 2026-08-26 wave silently dropped avatar initials and a progress value. Tooltip was NOT re-captured: its transform/translate-x fail the harness determinism self-check, which was verified to be pre-existing and independent of the mount (the same failure occurs with the mount reverted). Its committed capture and promotion are untouched.

diverging: the documented capture REFUSED and produced no record: Error: determinism self-check FAILED — UNSTABLE channels across double-run: transform, translate-x — witnesses: Tooltip:off__default @root (div|MuiPopper-root.MuiTooltip-popper.MuiTooltip-popperInteractive) transform: "matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 19, 53)" vs "matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 16, 53)" | Tooltip:off__default @root (div|MuiPopper-root.MuiTooltip-popper.MuiTooltip-popperInteractive) translate-x: "19px" vs "16px"
mui/tooltip.cause: THE CAPTURE REFUSES ITSELF — the sharpest row in this ledger, and an HONEST refusal by the engine's own determinism self-check. MUI's Tooltip mounts a Popper whose x offset is computed from the trigger's measured position, and two sweeps of the SAME configuration in one session disagree by 3px (19 vs 16). `extract/computed/run.ts` requires double-run byte-identity and stops. So `extract/computed/out/mui/tooltip` cannot be re-derived by anyone, on any machine, today — not because a fact was hand-written, but because the subject is not deterministic under the documented recipe. Cure: pin the Popper's placement in the capture config (a fixed anchor, the way the openDriver already pins `open`) so the offset stops being a function of layout timing, then recapture. Until then this record is a measurement nobody can repeat, and this row says so.
